items.q: What is the Test Pyramid?
o: Unit at the bottom, UI at the top — more fast cheap tests at the base
UI at the bottom, Unit at the top
Only two levels: manual and automated
items.e: Mike Cohn's pyramid: Unit (base) → Integration → UI (top). More tests at the bottom — faster and cheaper.

items.q: What is the Ice Cream Cone anti-pattern?
o: Many UI tests, few unit tests — an inverted pyramid
items.e: Ice Cream Cone — the anti-pattern where most tests are UI/manual and few are unit. Slow, expensive, unreliable.

items.q: What is smoke testing?
o: A shallow check of core functionality after a deploy
items.e: Smoke tests — a quick check that the system starts and basic functions work after a fresh deploy.

items.q: What is regression testing?
o: Verifying that new changes didn't break existing functionality
items.e: Regression testing verifies that existing functionality still works after code changes.

items.q: What is sanity testing?
o: A narrow deep check of a specific function after a fix
items.e: Sanity — narrow, focused testing of specific functionality, usually after a bugfix. A subset of regression.

items.q: What is exploratory testing?
o: Unstructured free investigation of the system without pre-written cases
items.e: Exploratory testing — simultaneous learning, test design and execution. Great for finding unexpected bugs.

items.q: What is End-to-End (E2E) testing?
o: Testing a complete user flow from start to finish
Testing the integration of two modules
items.e: E2E tests replay real user scenarios from start to finish through all layers of the system.

items.q: What is a flaky test?
o: A test that unpredictably passes or fails with no code changes
items.e: A flaky test is non-deterministic. Causes: race conditions, time dependencies, external services, execution order.

items.q: What is test data management?
o: A strategy for preparing, isolating and cleaning up test data
items.e: Test data management — approaches to creating, maintaining and cleaning data: fixtures, factories, builders, DB scripts.

items.q: What is the AAA pattern in tests?
o: Arrange-Act-Assert — the structure of a test method
items.e: AAA: Arrange (prepare data) → Act (perform the action) → Assert (verify the result). The standard for readable tests.

items.q: Which JUnit5 annotation marks a test method?
items.e: @Test from org.junit.jupiter.api.Test marks a method as a JUnit5 test.

items.q: Which JUnit5 annotation runs before every test?
items.e: @BeforeEach — replaces JUnit4's @Before. Runs before every test method in the class.

items.q: Which JUnit5 annotation runs once before all tests in a class?
items.e: @BeforeAll (a static method) — replaces JUnit4's @BeforeClass. Runs once for the whole class.

items.q: How do you skip a test in JUnit5?
items.e: @Disabled — replaces JUnit4's @Ignore. You can add a reason: @Disabled("reason").

items.q: How do you parameterize a test in JUnit5?
items.e: @ParameterizedTest together with @ValueSource, @CsvSource, @MethodSource etc. — parameterization in JUnit5.

items.q: What is @ExtendWith in JUnit5?
o: Registers an extension to extend test behavior
items.e: @ExtendWith(MyExtension.class) — the JUnit5 extension mechanism replacing JUnit4's @RunWith.

items.q: How do you set test execution order in JUnit5?
items.e: @TestMethodOrder on the class plus @Order(n) on methods give a deterministic execution order.

items.q: What is @DisplayName in JUnit5?
o: Sets a human-readable test name for reports
items.e: @DisplayName("Readable test description") is shown in reports and IDEs instead of the method name.

items.q: How do you group tests in JUnit5?
items.e: @Tag("smoke") on tests plus filtering via Maven/Gradle or the IDE lets you run subsets of tests.

items.q: What is assertThrows in JUnit5?
o: Verifies that a method throws the expected exception
Verifies that an exception is NOT thrown
items.e: assertThrows(Exception.class, () -> method()) returns the exception for further checks on its message etc.

items.q: Which TestNG annotation marks a test method?
items.e: @Test from org.testng.annotations.Test — the core TestNG annotation for marking a test method.

items.q: How do you define test groups in TestNG?
items.e: @Test(groups={"smoke","regression"}) — the groups attribute in @Test for grouping and selective runs.

items.q: How do you define a dependency between tests in TestNG?
items.e: dependsOnMethods or dependsOnGroups — the test runs only if the dependency passed.

items.q: What is a DataProvider in TestNG?
o: A method returning a data array for parameterized tests
items.e: @DataProvider(name="data") returns Object[][] — each row is a parameter set for one invocation of the test method.

items.q: How do you attach a DataProvider to a test method in TestNG?
items.e: @Test(dataProvider="data", dataProviderClass=DataClass.class) links the test to a DataProvider.

items.q: What is testng.xml?
o: A config file defining suites, tests, groups and run order
items.e: testng.xml — the TestNG suite configuration file: which classes/methods/groups to run and in what order.

items.q: What is ITestListener in TestNG?
o: An interface for intercepting test events (pass, fail, skip)
items.e: ITestListener with onTestSuccess, onTestFailure, onTestSkipped etc. — custom logic on test events.

items.q: How do you do soft assertions in TestNG?
items.e: SoftAssert collects failures without stopping; assertAll() at the end throws AssertionError with all of them.

items.q: Which Maven command runs tests?
items.e: mvn test runs unit tests. mvn verify — runs integration tests and quality checks.

items.q: Which Maven plugin runs TestNG/JUnit tests?
items.e: maven-surefire-plugin — the standard plugin for running unit tests during the test phase.

items.q: Which Maven plugin runs integration tests?
items.e: maven-failsafe-plugin runs *IT.java tests during the integration-test and verify phases.

items.q: How do you skip tests during a Maven build?
items.e: -DskipTests compiles but doesn't run. -Dmaven.test.skip=true neither compiles nor runs the tests.

items.q: What is pom.xml?
o: Project Object Model — the Maven project config file
items.e: pom.xml describes the project: dependencies, plugins, properties, profiles — the main Maven configuration file.

items.q: Which Gradle command runs tests?
items.e: gradle test runs the tests. gradle check additionally runs static analysis and other verifications.

items.q: What is the Gradle wrapper (gradlew)?
o: A script that downloads the required Gradle version automatically
items.e: gradlew/gradlew.bat — run Gradle without installing it; the wrapper downloads the right version automatically.

items.q: Which Git command creates a new branch and switches to it?
o: git branch branch && git checkout branch
items.e: git checkout -b and git switch -c — both create and switch to a new branch.

items.q: What is the difference between git merge and git rebase?
o: merge keeps the full history, rebase rewrites it linearly
merge is faster, rebase is slower
rebase keeps commits, merge deletes them
items.e: merge adds a merge commit preserving full history. rebase replays commits onto the tip of another branch — a cleaner linear history.

items.q: What is git stash?
o: Creates a new branch with the changes
items.e: git stash saves uncommitted changes to a stack. git stash pop brings them back.

items.q: What is git cherry-pick?
o: Applies a specific commit from another branch
items.e: git cherry-pick <hash> applies the changes of a specific commit onto the current branch without merging the whole branch.

items.q: What is .gitignore?
o: A file with patterns of files Git doesn't track
items.e: .gitignore lists files and folders (target/, .idea/, *.log) that Git ignores and doesn't include in commits.

items.q: What is CI (Continuous Integration)?
o: Automatic build and testing on every push
items.e: CI — frequently merging code with automatic builds and test runs to catch problems early.

items.q: What is CD (Continuous Delivery)?
o: Automatic preparation for deployment, but the deploy is manual
Fully automatic deployment without a human
items.e: Continuous Delivery — every change is ready for production deployment. The deploy itself is triggered manually (unlike Deployment).

items.q: What is Continuous Deployment?
o: Fully automatic deployment to production without human involvement
items.e: Continuous Deployment — every push that passes the tests is automatically deployed to production with no manual step.

items.q: Which file describes a pipeline in GitHub Actions?
items.e: GitHub Actions uses YAML files in .github/workflows/ to describe CI/CD pipelines.

items.q: What is the Jenkins pipeline config file called?
items.e: Jenkinsfile (Groovy DSL) — a declarative or scripted Jenkins pipeline description, usually in the repo root.

items.q: What is Docker in the context of testing?
o: Containerization for an isolated and reproducible test environment
items.e: Docker runs tests in isolated containers — the same environment locally and on the CI server.

items.q: What is a Dockerfile?
o: Instructions for building a Docker image
items.e: Dockerfile — a text file with FROM, RUN, COPY, CMD etc. commands for building your own Docker image.

items.q: What is docker-compose?
o: A tool for running several Docker containers together
items.e: docker-compose.yml describes multi-container apps: e.g. tests + a database + a mock server together.

items.q: What is the Page Object Model (POM)?
o: A pattern where every page is a separate class with locators and methods
items.e: POM separates UI interaction logic from test logic. Every page is a class with locators and action methods.

items.q: What is the main advantage of Page Object?
o: Centralized locators — when the UI changes you fix one place only
items.e: If a locator changes — you fix it only in the Page Object class, not in every test that uses it.

items.q: What is Page Factory in Selenium?
o: A mechanism to initialize WebElement fields via @FindBy annotations
items.e: PageFactory.initElements(driver, this) initializes @FindBy fields lazily via Java Proxy.

items.q: What is a Fluent Page Object?
o: Page methods return this or another Page Object for chained calls
A Page Object with async methods
items.e: Fluent POM: methods return a Page Object for a fluent API: loginPage.enterEmail(e).enterPassword(p).clickLogin().

items.q: What is the Singleton pattern in the WebDriver context?
o: One WebDriver instance per test run or thread
A WebDriver that runs a single test
A driver that can't be closed
A driver with a single window
items.e: WebDriver Singleton ensures one driver instance per thread. With parallel tests, ThreadLocal is used.

items.q: What is a ThreadLocal WebDriver?
o: Each thread gets its own WebDriver instance — for parallel runs
items.e: ThreadLocal<WebDriver> guarantees isolation: every parallel test gets its own WebDriver instance.

items.q: What is the Builder pattern in test data?
o: A step-by-step fluent API for creating complex test data objects
items.e: User.builder().name("John").email("j@t.com").role(ADMIN).build() — readable object creation without huge constructors.

items.q: What is the Factory pattern in tests?
o: A factory method for creating objects without binding to a concrete class
items.e: Factory hides creation details: WebDriverFactory.getDriver("chrome") returns the right driver.

items.q: What is the Strategy pattern in tests?
items.e: Strategy swaps behavior: LoginStrategy can be UILogin or APILogin — the tests don't know the difference.

items.q: Which Allure annotation adds a step to the report?
items.e: @Step("Step description") on a method — Allure automatically adds it as a report step with parameters.

items.q: Which Allure annotation adds a description to a test?
items.e: @Description("Detailed test description") adds a test case description to the Allure report.

items.q: Which Allure annotation links a test to an issue?
items.e: @Issue("BUG-123") and @Link(url, type=LinkType.ISSUE) — both add a link to the issue tracker.

items.q: How do you attach a screenshot to the Allure report manually?
items.e: Allure.addAttachment() and Allure.attach() — both attach files, screenshots and logs to the report.

items.q: Which Allure annotation sets test severity?
items.e: @Severity(SeverityLevel.BLOCKER/CRITICAL/NORMAL/MINOR/TRIVIAL) sets the test criticality level in the report.

items.q: Which Allure annotation adds a story?
items.e: @Epic → @Feature → @Story — the Allure grouping hierarchy: Epic > Feature > Story.

items.q: What is the difference between findElement and findElements in Selenium?
o: findElement — first match or NoSuchElementException, findElements — a list or an empty list
items.e: findElement throws NoSuchElementException when nothing is found. findElements returns an empty List without errors.

items.q: What is an Explicit Wait in Selenium?
o: WebDriverWait that waits for a specific condition until a timeout
An implicit wait for all elements
items.e: WebDriverWait + ExpectedConditions waits for a specific condition (visibilityOf, clickable) up to the given timeout.

items.q: What is an Implicit Wait?
o: A global element lookup timeout for the whole WebDriver
A wait for a specific element
items.e: driver.manage().timeouts().implicitlyWait() sets the element lookup time globally for all findElement calls.

items.q: Why is mixing Implicit and Explicit Waits discouraged?
o: Unpredictable behavior — the timeouts can add up
items.e: When mixed, the total timeout can become implicit + explicit, causing unpredictable delays.

items.q: What is the Actions class in Selenium?
o: A class for complex interactions: drag&drop, hover, keys
items.e: The Actions API performs low-level actions: moveToElement, clickAndHold, dragAndDrop, sendKeys and more.

items.q: How do you execute JavaScript in Selenium?
items.e: JavascriptExecutor.executeScript() runs arbitrary JS, e.g. for scrolling or clicking outside the viewport.

items.q: What is WebDriverManager?
o: A library that automatically downloads the right driver (chromedriver etc.)
items.e: io.github.bonigarcia:webdrivermanager detects the browser version and downloads the matching driver automatically.

items.q: What is the DRY principle in tests?
o: Don't Repeat Yourself — extract duplicated code into helpers/methods
Debug Run Yield — starting a debug run
Daily Run Yesterday — running yesterday's tests
items.e: DRY: don't duplicate code — move repeated actions into Page Object methods, helpers, base classes.

items.q: What is the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) in tests?
o: Each test verifies one specific behavior
items.e: SRP in tests: one test — one behavior under test. Easier to find the cause of a failure.

items.q: What is test isolation?
o: Tests don't depend on each other and can run in any order
Tests run isolated from the network
items.e: An isolated test leaves no state affecting other tests and doesn't depend on execution order.

items.q: What are test doubles?
o: The umbrella term for mock, stub, spy, fake, dummy
items.e: Test doubles: Dummy (placeholder), Stub (fixed response), Spy (wrapper), Mock (call verification), Fake (simplified implementation).

items.q: What is a Mock in testing?
o: An object that verifies methods were called with the right parameters
An object with a fixed response
A real object that logs calls
items.e: A Mock verifies behavior: checks that a method was called, how many times and with which arguments.

items.q: What is a Stub in testing?
o: Returns a predefined response without verifying calls
A wrapper over a real object
items.e: A Stub returns fixed data (e.g. a canned HTTP response) without checking how it was called.

items.q: What is WireMock?
o: A tool for mocking an HTTP server when testing APIs
A mocking framework for Java objects
items.e: WireMock runs a local HTTP server responding by defined rules — for isolated testing of API clients.

items.q: What is Mockito?
o: A Java framework for creating mock objects
items.e: Mockito — the most popular Java mocking framework: @Mock, when().thenReturn(), verify() and more.

items.q: What is the HTTP GET method?
o: Retrieves a resource, idempotent, no request body
items.e: GET retrieves a resource. Idempotent and safe — doesn't change server state. Has no request body.

items.q: Which HTTP status means "Created"?
items.e: 201 Created — the resource was created successfully (usually in response to POST). Often includes a Location header.

items.q: Which HTTP status means "No Content"?
items.e: 204 No Content — the request succeeded but the response has no body. Typical for DELETE or PUT.

items.q: Which HTTP status means "Unauthorized"?
items.e: 401 Unauthorized — authentication required. 403 Forbidden — authenticated but no access rights.

items.q: What is idempotency of HTTP methods?
o: A repeated call gives the same result as a single one
The method returns the same response
items.e: Idempotent methods: GET, PUT, DELETE, HEAD. Not idempotent: POST (each call may create a new resource).

items.q: What is REST (Representational State Transfer)?
o: An architectural style for distributed systems over HTTP
items.e: REST — an architectural style (not a protocol): stateless, client-server, uniform interface, cacheable, layered system.

items.q: What is JSON Schema?
o: A specification for describing the structure and validating JSON documents
items.e: JSON Schema describes the expected JSON structure: field types, required fields, formats — for automatic validation.

items.q: What is shift-left testing?
o: Involving testing earlier in the development cycle
Moving tests to the next sprint
items.e: Shift-left: testers get involved at the requirements and design stage, not only after development.

items.q: What is coverage in testing?
o: The percentage of code/requirements covered by tests
items.e: Coverage: code coverage (lines/branches covered by tests), requirements coverage (requirements covered by test cases).

items.q: What is 100% code coverage and why isn't it always the goal?
o: Every line executed, but it doesn't guarantee correct logic
items.e: 100% code coverage means every line ran, not that all input combinations and edge cases were verified.

items.q: What is Boundary Value Analysis (BVA)?
o: Testing the boundary values of an input range
items.e: BVA: for a 1-100 field test 0, 1, 2, 99, 100, 101 — errors cluster at the range boundaries.

items.q: What is Equivalence Partitioning?
o: Splitting inputs into classes with identical behavior
items.e: EP: if a field accepts 1-100, test one value from each class: negatives, 1-100, >100 — instead of trying them all.

items.q: What is decision table testing?
o: A table of conditions and corresponding actions to cover all combinations
items.e: A decision table enumerates all combinations of conditions and expected actions — useful for complex business logic.

items.q: What is state transition testing?
items.e: State transition: build a state diagram and verify all valid and invalid transitions between states.

items.q: What is Requirements Traceability?
o: The link between requirements and the test cases verifying them
items.e: A Traceability Matrix shows which test cases cover which requirements — for coverage assessment and impact analysis.

items.q: What is a bug report?
o: A structured defect description: steps to reproduce, expected/actual result, environment
An automatic CI report with run logs, coverage, duration and failed assertions
A short message to the developer without expected result, environment or exact steps
A document with a business requirement, acceptance criteria and a roadmap
items.e: A good bug report: Title, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Result, Actual Result, Environment, Severity, Priority, Attachments.

items.q: What is the difference between bug Severity and Priority?
o: Severity — impact on the system, Priority — business urgency of the fix
Severity is for QA, Priority is for the PM
items.e: Severity: how technically critical the bug is (blocker/critical/major/minor). Priority: how urgently it must be fixed (business).

items.q: What is performance testing?
o: Checking speed, stability and scalability under load
items.e: Performance testing includes: Load (normal load), Stress (peak), Endurance (sustained), Spike (sudden growth).

items.q: Which tools are used for load testing?
items.e: JMeter (Apache), Gatling (Scala DSL), k6 (JavaScript) — popular load testing tools.

items.q: What are the FIRST principles for unit tests?
items.e: FIRST: Fast, Independent, Repeatable, Self-validating, Timely.

items.q: What is WireMock stubbing?
o: Configuring WireMock to return a given response to a request
items.e: stubFor(get(urlEqualTo("/api")).willReturn(aResponse().withStatus(200).withBody(json))) — a WireMock stub.

items.q: What is a Postman Collection?
o: A set of HTTP requests, tests and variables for API documentation and automation
items.e: A Postman Collection — an organized group of requests with pre-request scripts, tests (pm.test), variables and environments.

items.q: What is Testcontainers?
o: A Java library for running Docker containers in tests (DBs, Kafka etc.)
A container for storing test data
items.e: Testcontainers starts real Docker containers (PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka) right inside tests — no mocks.

items.q: What is SonarQube?
o: A code quality platform: bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells
items.e: SonarQube statically analyzes Java/JS/etc code: finds bugs, security vulnerabilities, duplications, code coverage.

items.q: What is code review in the context of tests?
o: Peer review of test code before merging
items.e: Reviewing test code matters as much as production code: it checks logic, readability and edge case coverage.

items.q: What is a test plan?
o: A document describing the scope, approach, resources and schedule of testing
items.e: Test Plan (IEEE 829): testing scope, approaches, risks, resources, entry/exit criteria, schedule and responsibilities.

items.q: What are Exit Criteria in testing?
o: Conditions under which testing is considered complete
items.e: Exit Criteria: e.g. 95% of test cases passed, 0 critical bugs open, coverage > 80%. They define when you can release.
